title: Accords commence and capital moves while substantive terms are still deferred to a future Atlas iteration
content:
A recurring sentence appears in Accords 4 through 9: "Additional detail regarding the substantive terms ... will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas, as agreed by the Parties to the Accord." Keel's tokenomics are explicitly unspecified — "The tokenomics for Keel will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas" (A.2.8.2.3.2.2). Skybase's total token supply, treasury allocation, and Sky-retained amount are all deferred (A.2.8.2.7.2.1.1 through .1.2.2). Osero's Sky-retained 322,222,222 tokens have no stated distribution (A.2.8.2.6.2.1.2.2).

Yet in the same documents the duration has already commenced and the Genesis Capital Allocation is already authorized: 10M USDS for Keel, 21M for Obex, 25M each for Amatsu and Ozone.

This is a deliberate sequencing choice rather than sloppiness — it lets Sky capitalize a counterparty on the strength of its role and party structure, and negotiate token economics later once the venture has substance. But it inverts the usual protection ordering. The party whose terms are unspecified has already been funded, so Sky's leverage in the deferred negotiation is weaker than it would have been pre-funding, and the counterparty's obligations are thinner than its receipts.

It also means an Accord section that looks complete may be a placeholder; the absence of a Tokenomics figure is not evidence that no token exists.
description: Five of the nine Accords defer their substantive terms or tokenomics entirely, yet duration has already started and Genesis Capital Allocations are already authorized
